title: Inertia and weight of a pair bound through the field, full grip

key_results.statement: Half-gap $\sigma_iR_i=\frac{N_f}2[\varepsilon_0(g_i)-\varepsilon_0(-g_i)]=ng_i[1+O(\eta^2)]$, $c_i^2=\sigma_iR_i/\mu_i=\tau_i^2[1+O(N_f\eta^2)]$, the part $M_i^o$ of the mutual term odd in $g_i$ ($M_1^o=M_2^o=B[1+O(\eta)]$), and the bond average $\bar f(\rho)=\frac14[f(\rho-1)+2f(\rho)+f(\rho+1)]$.

Full grip, band regime $\max\tau_i\ll d$: the band contract is (2.10)/(6.1), and the gap of the double step of $b_i$ across the relative bond $\rho$ from $r=\rho\mp1$ is $\Delta_i(r;\rho)=2\sigma_iR_i+M_i^o(r)+M_i^o(\rho)+M_i^e(r)-M_i^e(\rho)$.
Local inertia of each body: $m_i(\rho)=\mu_i+\bar M_i^o(\rho)/c_i^2+O(|\mu_i|\eta^2)=\mu_i+\bar B(\rho)/\tau_i^2\,[1+O(\eta)]$; (6.5) and (6.6) hold for the full grip.

The selected level is bound at $r\approx0$ iff $\tau_1^2g_2+\tau_2^2g_1>0$ ($g_i=\sigma_i\gamma_iM_i$): lowest if both $g_i>0$, highest for opposite signs, never for both $g_i<0$; otherwise the extreme level sits at $r\approx L/2$ (binding regime $w\ll L$, tuned near-zero cases excluded).

$D_0=1/E_b''(0)-\mu_1-\mu_2=D^{\rm lat}+D^{\rm mark}$ with $D^{\rm lat}=(\mu_1+\mu_2)(1-\beta_0)/\beta_0$ and $D^{\rm mark}=\beta_0^{-2}\sum_\rho b_0\sum_i\bar M_i^o/c_i^2=(\tau_1^{-2}+\tau_2^{-2})\beta_0^{-2}\sum_\rho b_0\bar B\,[1+O(\eta)]$, i.e. (6.8) with $s_c=+1$, $c_i=\tau_i$, up to $O((|\mu_1|+|\mu_2|)[\eta^2+\frac{\tau^2}{d^2}(\eta+1-\beta_0)])$ and the ring remainder.
Cost of the bond: $\Delta E_0=\langle M\rangle_0+K_0[1+O(\eta)]$, $K_0=\frac14(\mu_1^{-1}+\mu_2^{-1})(1-\beta_0)$.

Item 3 (i): $D_0\neq\Delta E_0/v^2$ for $v=\tau_1$ or $\tau_2$; the lattice part $4\mu_1\mu_2K_0/\beta_0$ exceeds $K_0/v^2$ by a factor $\ge d^2/\tau_j^2\gg1$ and the mark part exceeds $\langle M\rangle_0/v^2$ by $\langle M\rangle_0/\tau_j^2$; equality only on a tuned surface, which exists only for $g_1,g_2>0$.

Item 3 (ii), regime $1-\beta_0\ll\eta\ll1$: $D_0=(\tau_1^{-2}+\tau_2^{-2})\Delta E_0[1+O(\eta,(1-\beta_0)/\eta,\tau^2/d^2)]$, i.e. $2\Delta E_0/v^2$ for $\tau_1=\tau_2=v$, not $\Delta E_0/v^2$; it approaches $\Delta E_0/\tau_i^2$ only as $\tau_i/\tau_j\to0$.
Weight gradient of a single held body on the ring: $W_i'=\phi'[ng_i+2\kappa_sC_i^{(2)}]$ up to relative $O(\eta^2)$, $C_i^{(2)}=-ng_i^2\ell_0/t_f$, $\kappa_s=(L^2(1-2u)^2+2)/(L^2-1)$, $u=s/L$.
Bond part of the weight gradient of the selected level: $W_b'=\phi'[2\kappa_sB(0)+\langle V\rangle_0-K_0][1+O(\eta/\kappa_s)]$ for a source at distance $s\gg w$.

Exactly $\Gamma_{\rm pair}=(\mu_1\Gamma_1+\mu_2\Gamma_2+D_0\Gamma_b)/(\mu_1+\mu_2+D_0)$ with $\Gamma_b=W_b'/D_0$; $\Gamma_i=\tau_i^2\phi'[1-2\kappa_sg_i\ell_0/t_f+O(\eta^2,N_f\eta^2,\tau^2/d^2)]$; at leading order $\Gamma_{\rm pair}=\beta_0\bar\Gamma$, equal to $\Gamma_1=\Gamma_2$ (for $1-\beta_0\to0$) iff $\tau_1=\tau_2$.

Regime $1-\beta_0\ll\eta$: $\Gamma_b=2\kappa_s\phi'/(\tau_1^{-2}+\tau_2^{-2})$; for $\tau_1=\tau_2$ the binding cost is weighed in the same proportion as its inertia only as $u\to0$, at finite $u$ less by $\kappa_s<1$, and $\Gamma_{\rm pair}-\bar\Gamma=4(1-\kappa_s)g_1g_2\ell_0\tau^2\phi'/(t_f(g_1+g_2))$.

At fixed $n,\gamma_i,M_i,\tau_i$: mark quantities scale as $t_f^{-1}$, lattice quantities as $t_f^{-2/3}$ ($w\gg1$), $D^{\rm lat}/|D^{\rm mark}|\propto t_f^{1/3}$, while $D^{\rm mark}/\Delta E_0\to\tau_1^{-2}+\tau_2^{-2}$ and $\Gamma_b/\Gamma_i\to2\kappa_s/(1+\tau_i^2/\tau_j^2)$ do not depend on $t_f$.

definitions.name: part of the mutual term odd in one coupling
local inertia of a body in the pair
lattice and mark parts of the pair inertia
second-order even part of the cost
fall factors of body, pair and bond
distance of the group to the other held levels

open_issues: The code check has N_f = 1, so the regime of item 3 (ii) is reached only moderately (D_lat/|D_mark| = 0.21 at L = 128, η = 0.15); the O(η) corrections have large coefficients (⟨M1odd+M2odd⟩/⟨M⟩ = 2.11 at η = 0.05, 2.40 at η = 0.15).
The kinetic weight −K0 φ′ in (7.10) is derived, not checked: the code uses held weights.
The fall itself (time evolution) is not simulated; the fall factor is taken from (5.14), (6.13).
The factor κ_s is a property of the ring (zero mode); other geometries (tori) are out of scope.
c_i² = τ_i²[1+O(N_f η²)] is an estimate of the overlap corrections of (5.3), not derived in detail.

consistency_checks.check: Dimensions of (7.3), (7.5), (7.7), (7.8) and of the fall factors
Limit g2 → 0: mark and bond terms vanish linearly, m1 → μ1, w → ∞, (7.9) reduces to (4.5)
Coincident held pair r = 0 weighs as one coupling g1+g2 (C1+C2+B(0) = C_G)
